Name: Scientific Enrichment Month (SEM)
Subject: Science
Description: The Scientific Enrichment Month program at the Herbert Irving Comprehensive Cancer Center at Columbia University is a free enrichment program where student can gain knowledge on cancer science and biomedical research. This program has a registration instead of an application, so while the due date is in June 19, 2026, the capacity may be met before then. Participants of this program can learn from virtual lectures, workshops, and discussions with real scientists and medical professionals. This program is perfect for those who want an introduction to research careers, scientific inquiry, and health sciences. In addition, this program provides high school students with professional development and mentorship opportunities. If interested in biology, medicine, or research careers to gain early exposure to the field, make sure to check out this great opportunity.

Name: Ocean Guardian Youth Ambassador Program
Subject: Science
Description: Interested in marine life and the conservation of our oceans? If yes, then the Ocean Guardian Youth Ambassador program is for you! This virtual program, made for anyone age 13-18, discusses every aspect of ocean conservation. Not only does the Ambassador program consist of an abundance of opportunities to collaborate with marine scientists and experts in the field, but it will also allow for you to gain hands-on experience in leadership. Part of the Ambassadors program includes the monthly webinars, where you have the chance to learn about threats to the ocean, ocean conservation efforts, further programs and careers in regards to marine science, alongside other opportunities to emphasize leadership. The program runs from January to December, and applications for the 2026-2027 year will open on November 13th and close on January 3rd.

Name: Horizons Polaris
Subject: Computer Science
Description: Horizons Polaris, hosted by Hack Club, is a beginner-friendly, in-person hackathon taking place from August 7–9 in Toronto, open to middle school and high school students from around the world. Travel grants are available to help cover transportation costs for students outside of Toronto, making it possible for participants from anywhere to attend without being limited by distance or travel expenses. To earn an invitation, students must complete 35 hours of coding between April and August, and no prior programming experience is required, making the program accessible to complete beginners as well as more experienced coders. Over the three-day event, attendees will collaborate on projects, learn new technical skills, and participate in a creative, supportive environment focused on building and experimentation. All participants will receive free accommodations, meals, and merch throughout the event, allowing them to focus fully on the experience. There will also be opportunities to showcase projects, receive feedback, and compete for prizes, while connecting with students from diverse backgrounds and locations.

Name: Teen Techies Volunteership
Subject: Technology
Description: The Teen Techies Volunteership is a half-yearlong volunteering program for anyone interested in IT or fields relating to the usage of computers. During this internship, students will learn new computer skills over a two-week fall technology institute, and they will also assist library staff with computer troubleshooting and training workshops. Following this, students will embark upon a six-month long period of volunteering for three hours weekly. During the volunteership, students will be required to attend two Volunteer Forms, which serve as a common medium for students to assist one another and discuss challenges or successes. Students must live in Brooklyn, be 14-18 years old, and have a recommender in order to apply. The deadline for submission is June 19th, so be sure to apply as soon as possible!

Name: WCEJ Thornton Foundation Music & Art Scholarship
Subject: Arts
Description: The WCEJ Thornton Foundation Music and Art Scholarship is a $30,000 scholarship with 30 winners that is managed by the WCEJ Thornton Foundation. In order to apply, students must be either a high school senior or a graduate who will be enrolled in higher education by fall of this year. Preferences will be given to students who are pursuing art majors. The application process requires a 150-400 word response to a given prompt. For this scholarship, students must respond to how they plan to make a positive impact on the world through their art or music. Additionally, it is recommended to submit sample artwork alongside your application. The application is due on July 1st, and winners will be announced on August 1st.

Name: Julia Wood History Essay Competition
Subject: History
Description: The Julia Wood History Essay Competition, organized by St Hugh’s College at the University of Oxford, is a prestigious annual history essay competition established in 1971 in memory of alumna Julia Wood, where students choose their own historical topic and submit an original 2,000-4,000 word essay demonstrating university-level research, analysis, and argumentation, judged by Oxford academics, with winners receiving cash prizes up to £600 (often split), publication on the college website, certificates, and strong recognition for university applications. The 2026 competition is currently open, with essays due by 5pm on Friday, July 24, 2026 (date to be confirmed), and results announced by the end of September 2026 with winning essays published online. It is open worldwide to Year 12/13 (ages 16-18) students who have been in sixth form for less than two years, requiring strong independent research skills and a fully referenced academic essay. Submissions are made online as a PDF through the St Hugh’s College website, with no in-person requirements, and winners receive certificates and prizes digitally.

Name: Philip and Jacqueline Benincasa Education Scholarship
Subject: Education
Description: The Philip and Jacqueline Benincasa Education Scholarship is a $6000 scholarship with two winners. The scholarship was created in memory of Philip and Jacqueline Benincasa, who were parents that recently passed away. The scholarship is aimed at any high school senior, graduate, or undergraduate in Massachusetts who is majoring in education or education administration. In order to apply, students will need to respond to a given prompt. The prompt for this scholarship is a 400-600 word response to the question of why higher education is important as well as why the student would pursue an education major. The application deadline is October 30th, and winners will be announced on December 1st.

Name: Science and Engineering Apprentice Program
Subject: STEM
Description: The Science and Engineering Apprentice Program (SEAP) is an eight-week long summer program for students who have exceptional interest in science and mathematics. During the program, students will have the opportunity to work with research mentors in laboratory settings that are typically not available in school settings. Over 25 different laboratories partake in this program, all in varied locations. Students are responsible for their own transportation, and stipends are given for the program based on the level of experience (e.g. first-year interns receive $4,000, while returning interns receive $4,500). Students must be at least 16 years old by the time of the internship, must have completed at least 9th grade, and must be a U.S. citizen.

Name: KinderKids Early Childhood Excellence Scholarship
Subject: Education
Description: The KinderKids Early Childhood Excellence Scholarship is a fabulous scholarship opportunity for anyone seeking to pursue a degree in early childhood education or elementary education. In order to apply, students must be a high school graduate in the class of 2026, alongside being in Baldwin County, Alabama. Alongside these prerequisites, students must respond to a prompt regarding why they chose to pursue a degree in early childhood education or elementary education and why strong educators are necessary for building a thriving community. Responses should be 400-600 words in length, and should also include the significance of education and personal reasons for pursuing the field. Student responses should highlight the understanding of the overarching significance of the profession and its facets in leadership. The application is due on July 23rd, and the two winners will be announced on August 24th.

Name: Chef Marco “Gabby” Pantano Memorial Scholarship
Subject: Culinary
Description: The Chef Marco “Gabby” Pantano Memorial Scholarship is a $1,300 scholarship founded in honor of the late chef Marco Pantano. Pantano spent 35 years of his life invested in the culinary arts, and was best known for his passion of his career. In order to apply for this scholarship, students must be either a current culinary arts student or a high school senior attempting to pursue the culinary arts or higher education. Alongside these prerequisites, students must respond to a prompt asking for the reasoning behind pursuing an education in the culinary arts and future career goals with a 400-600 word response. The application is due September 3rd, and winners will be announced on October 4th.

Name: Voice of Democracy Audio-Essay Competition
Subject: Audio Essay
Description: The Voice of Democracy Audio-Essay Competition is a prestigious, annual competition with nearly $2.1 million in winnings for 40,000 students. The national first place winner will receive a $35,000 scholarship to the American university of their choice, with other scholarships varying from $1000 to $15,000. This competition is open to all students from grades 9-12, and students must submit a 3 to 5 minute long audio essay answering the prompt of how you are showing patriotism and support for the United States. The rubric for the audio-essay is split into 3 categories: originality, which is worth 30 points; content, which is worth 35 points; and delivery, which is also worth 35 points. The submission deadline is October 31st, so be sure to submit soon!

Name: Borgen Project Internships
Subject: N/A
Description: The Borgen Project, a global nonprofit organization that seeks to end global poverty problems, offers work-at-home internship opportunities for anyone seeking to spread awareness and promote change. The Project offers four unique internships: a Political Affairs internship that deals with making poverty a focus of foreign policy; a Writer/Journalist internship that deals with content creation for the Borgen Magazine and Project Blog; a Social Media/Digital Marketing internship that deals with heightening awareness; and a Nonprofit Leadership internship that lets interns learn how to make nonprofits for themselves. The Borgen Project follows a rolling-basis admission style for internships, but the themes of the given internships change monthly. This is a strong opportunity for anyone seeking to gain experience in foreign affairs or international relations.

Name: Joanne Pransky Celebration of Women in Robotics
Subject: Robotics
Description: The Joanne Pransky Celebration of Women in Robotics scholarship is a $10,000 opportunity for any student identifying as female alongside being in high school, undergraduate, or graduate program. Inspired by Joanne Pransky’s impact on robotics, the scholarship aims to honor the impact of Joanne Pransky by giving support to women in robotics. In order to apply, students must write a 500-1000 word short story about the challenges or opportunities of robotics in the future. There are 10 winners, and the deadline to submit is August 30th. Winners will be drawn on October 1st!

Name: Kelly Mays Legacy Scholarship
Subject: Psychology
Description: The Kelly Mays Legacy scholarship is a $750 opportunity created in honor of Kelly Mays, who was a strong advocate for supporting victims of domestic violence. This scholarship is open to any high school senior, college freshman, or college sophomore in Michigan pursuing a four-year degree in psychology or social work. In order to apply, students must write a 400-600 word response to a given prompt. The prompt for this year’s scholarship is to describe a personal experience, moment, or realization that inspired interest in the field of psychology or social work, and how one may use that education to advocate for others and catalyze change. The deadline for submission is July 31st, and winners will be announced on September 1st.

Name: USESO Leadership in Earth and Environmental Sciences (LEES) Program
Subject: Science
Description: The USESO LEES Program is a virtual summer camp for high school students focused on Earth and environmental sciences, where participants learn through discussions, collaboration, and expert-led sessions covering topics such as the IPCC, environmental law and ESG standards, indoor air quality in public housing, and the Superfund Research Program, while also engaging in activities involving creativity, individual agency, competition, outdoor field studies, and conversations with industry experts and faculty. LEES 2026 runs from July 13-17, 2026, with the registration deadline being open until June 19, 2026. To be eligible for registration students must be entering grades 8-12 in the fall of 2025 and are permanent residents of the USA (green card holder or US citizen). There is a tuition fee of 200$ per person, however for students to whom the tuition fee poses a significant financial barrier, partial or full waivers are available.

Name: Aspiring Scholars Directed Research Program
Subject: Science
Description: The Aspiring Scholars Directed Research Program (ASDRP) is a competitive research program for high school students that allows participants to work as student researchers, with admissions based primarily on the quality of the application rather than recommendation letters. Applications are accepted three times per year for summer, fall, and spring entry, with deadlines listed on the official application schedule and late applications not considered, while the website references Summer 2025 deadlines as an example of the schedule structure. The program is open to students currently enrolled in or entering grades 9-12, including applicants from the Bay Area, elsewhere in California, and other U.S. states. ASDRP is based in the Bay Area, California, with applications submitted online through the ASDRP application portal.

Name: New York Women in Accounting Scholarship
Subject: Business
Description: The New York Women in Accounting scholarship is a $1,500 opportunity with two winners. Accounting is an important field  that faces underrepresentation of both women and people of color, and as a result, many clients may not feel seen. Through this scholarship, a more cohesive and diverse workforce will be created. Students who are female or people of color are eligible to apply, but only if they are studying accounting in New York. Alongside these prerequisites, applicants must also write a 400-600 word response to a given prompt, which asks for why applicants want to pursue a degree or career in accounting. Of the two winners, the first place winner will receive $1000 and the second place winner will receive $500. The deadline to submit is July 2nd.

Name: Women in Elementary Education Scholarship
Subject: Education
Description: The Women in Elementary Education scholarship is a $3,000 opportunity with three winners. The impact of education starts extremely early, with childhood educators setting the scene of schooling for the rest of the years of a student’s academic odyssey. This scholarship aims to support students who are passionate in shaping the next generation’s minds. Female high school seniors in Washington, Oregon, or California are eligible to apply for this opportunity. Alongside these requisites, applicants are also required to answer a given essay prompt. In 400-600 words, students are expected to respond to how they plan to make a positive impact in educating elementary children, alongside how they attempt to promote the enjoyment of learning. The deadline for submission is August 9th, and winners will be announced on September 10th.

Name: Aaron and Ruby Dicks Scholarship
Subject: N/A
Description: The Aaron and Ruby Dicks scholarship is a $1,000 scholarship with one winner. The scholarship was created in order to honor Aaron and Ruby Dicks, who were a couple from South Carolina that was known in their community for their hard work and determination. Any Black high school senior or undergraduate may apply to the scholarship, and a response to a given essay prompt is required in order to apply. For the essay, applicants must respond with what they have learned from books and how they’ve informed the impacts that they desire. The deadline is August 29th, and winners will be announced on September 30th.

Name: The Bronx Museum — Teen Summer Program
Subject: Arts
Description: The 2026 Teen Summer program at The Bronx Museum is a free four-week arts-intensive opportunity for NYC high school students ages 14–19 who are interested in art, museums, and creative culture. Led by Bronx Museum Educators, the program gives participants the chance to explore New York City’s art scene while learning about the curatorial process and how museums can amplify community voices. During this year’s program, students will work together to curate an exhibition using artwork from The Bronx Museum’s permanent collection. Teen Summer meets Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays from 1:00 PM to 5:00 PM from late July through mid-August 2026, with most sessions taking place on-site at The Bronx Museum. Participants are paid to attend, making it both a creative and professional development opportunity for teens interested in art, leadership, public engagement, or museum work. Applications open on Friday, May 22, 2026 at 12:00 PM ET and close on Sunday, July 5, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. There is no cost to participate, making it an accessible opportunity for students looking to gain hands-on experience in the arts and museum field.

Name: New York Academy of Sciences — The Junior Academy
Subject: Education
Description: The Junior Academy is a free virtual STEM program for students ages 13–17 that connects participants with an international community of peers, STEM experts, and industry leaders through the New York Academy of Sciences’ online platform, Launchpad. Students work in teams to complete Innovation Challenges sponsored by leading companies, where they collaborate to design solutions to real-world problems while receiving mentorship from STEM professionals and guidance in areas such as research methods, design thinking, and data analysis. Participants commit about three to four hours per week during challenge periods, and all programming is conducted in English. The program is completely free and accessible from anywhere in the world. Applications for the Fall 2026 cohort open on April 1, 2026 and close on July 2, 2026, with admission decisions released on August 31, 2026.

Name: Jersey City Free Public Library + Urban Word NYC — Youth Poet Laureate Program
Subject: Writing
Description: The Youth Poet Laureate Program, hosted by the Jersey City Free Public Library in partnership with Urban Word NYC, is a free poetry and leadership opportunity for students ages 13–18 who are passionate about creative writing, spoken word, and community engagement. The program recognizes young writers who use poetry to express themselves and advocate for issues affecting their communities. Finalists receive mentorship, workshops, and performance opportunities, while the selected Youth Poet Laureate earns a $500 award and serves as a literary ambassador for local youth. The competition is open to teens in the New York City and Jersey City area, and there is no cost to apply or participate. Applications for the 2026 program close on June 30, 2026, making it a valuable opportunity for students interested in poetry, public speaking, leadership, and the arts.

Name: Columbia Political Review Essay Contest
Subject: Writing
Description: The Columbia Essay Contest, organized by the Columbia Political Review (CPR), is an annual high school essay competition created to encourage politically engaged writing and amplify student voices worldwide, with the 2026 prompt asking students to examine young people’s dissatisfaction with liberal democracy and propose an alternative model of political participation while discussing its benefits and risks (full prompt on their website), and submissions judged based on clarity, concision, cohesion, argument strength, use of evidence, and consistency in style and tone. Essays must be submitted by July 1, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET, with only one submission allowed per student and no late submissions accepted. The contest is open to all high school students worldwide. Submissions are completed online as PDFs through the Columbia Political Review contest portal, and the competition is affiliated with Columbia University through CPR.

Name: International Psychology Olympiad
Subject: Psychology
Description: The International Psychology Olympiad (IPsyO) is an annual competition for high school students designed to identify and nurture talented students in psychology by challenging participants to deepen their understanding, originality, and creativity in the field through a series of tests, exams, and presentations. The registration deadline for the 2026 competition is July 1, 2026, with the first Grand Test taking place on July 11, 2026. It is open to high school students from the 80 eligible countries listed on the organization’s website who are currently enrolled in secondary or pre-collegiate education and who will graduate the year after the event or later, while fresh graduates, gap year students, and university students are not eligible. The competition is conducted entirely online, with exams completed through a dedicated testing platform and presentations submitted as videos, allowing participation from students around the world.

Name: RodentPro.com® Animal Advocate Scholarship
Subject: Pre-Vet
Description: The RodentPro.com Animal Advocate scholarship is a $1,000 opportunity for anyone pursuing a career of study involving the welfare of animals. Rodent Pro is a company that proudly supports animal rehabilitation centers, and aimed to promote animal welfare in the leaders of tomorrow through this scholarship. In order to apply, students must be incoming college freshmen or a current undergraduate student with a 3.0 GPA or more, and also must pursue a field of study which involves caring for animals. Acceptable fields of study include, but are not limited to, animal science, pre-vet tracks, veterinary science, and zoology. Alongside these prerequisites, applicants must respond to a given 400-600 word essay prompt regarding the role of animal care and welfare and how they envision contributions to their fields. The deadline to submit is October 5th, and the winner will be announced on November 6th.

Name: Mattie's Way Memorial Scholarship
Subject: Psychology
Description: The Mattie’s Way Memorial scholarship is a $1,000 opportunity for any student interested in pursuing a career in psychology. This scholarship was made in memory of Matthew “Mattie” Wilmoth, who tragically committed suicide in 2022 at the age of 17. Alongside this, the scholarship aims to raise awareness and reduce the stigmatization of mental health. In order to apply, students must be incoming college freshmen, located in West Virginia, Georgia, or Alabama, and majoring in psychology or counseling. Additionally, applicants must also respond to a given essay prompt about themselves and why they are passionate about psychology. The deadline to submit is May 10th, 2027, and the winner will be announced on June 1st, 2027.

Name: Map Free City (MFC)
Subject: Arts
Description: Map Free City (MFC) is a free summer arts program for New York City teens that provides participants with the opportunity to explore the city's vibrant arts and culture scene while developing skills in critical thinking, discussion, writing, and media creation. Through the program, students attend theater, dance, and music performances, visit artist studios, galleries, and museums, create digital media content in response to the art they experience, and publish reviews on ArtsConnection's online blog, The JAR. Participants also learn to navigate New York City independently while collaborating with fellow students who share an interest in the arts. The program consists of 12 sessions over four weeks and will run from July 7 through July 30, 2026, with workshops taking place from 2:00 PM to 4:30 PM on July 7, 8, 9, 14, 15, 16, 21, 22, 23, 28, 29, and 30. While ArtsConnection has announced that Map Free City will return in July 2026, an official application deadline has not yet been released. There is no cost to participate, making it an excellent opportunity for teens interested in visual arts, theater, dance, music, journalism, media production, or arts criticism to engage with New York City's cultural landscape while building creative and communication skills.

Name: Y Leaders at Freedom School Summer Leadership Bootcamp
Subject: Education
Description: The Y Leaders at Freedom School Summer Leadership Bootcamp is a free two-week leadership program for girls in grades 8–12 from Westchester County. Hosted by the YWCA White Plains & Central Westchester, the program will run from July 6–17, 2026, Monday through Friday from 10:00 AM to 3:00 PM at 515 North Street in White Plains, New York. Participants will develop leadership skills through workshops focused on confidence building, communication, and self-expression while exploring visual arts, journaling, mindfulness, and theater-based activities. Students will also support younger scholars by reading to K–5 students, leading enrichment programs, and participating in youth-led social action projects. By the end of the program, participants will have gained leadership experience, completed creative projects, and built connections with other students. There is no cost to participate, and applications are accepted on a first-come, first-served basis until all available spots are filled.

Name: Dia Teens
Subject: Arts
Description: Dia Teens is a free arts and leadership program hosted by the Dia Art Foundation at Dia Beacon for high school students interested in contemporary art, creative thinking, and community engagement. Participants work with professional artists and peers to create original projects while developing skills in critical thinking, collaboration, and self-expression. The Summer Intensive runs from July 7–August 14, 2026, meeting Tuesdays through Fridays from 11:00 AM to 3:00 PM, with additional field trips throughout the program. Students accepted into Dia Teens must commit to the full program year, including the 2026–2027 academic year. The program provides free transportation assistance, lunch, snacks, materials, and semester stipends for participants in good standing. Applicants must have completed at least one year of high school, and preference is given to Hudson Valley residents. The application deadline is June 21, 2026, with group interviews taking place on June 24, 2026.

Name: Chinese Dollars for Scholars College Prep Program
Subject: College Prep
Description: The Dollars for Scholars College Prep program is a valuable opportunity for any rising high school seniors to gain assistance with the upcoming college admissions cycle. Students will be able to have monthly workshops and office hours with Dollars for Scholars alumna who have previously worked in college admissions in the UCs, Cornell, and many other prestigious schools. In order to join, students must be of Chinese descent, starting their senior year of high school in Fall, living in the tri-state area, having a strong academic standing of above a 3.5 GPA on a 4.0 scale as well as a rigorous course load, and being motivated. Alongside these prerequisites, applicants must also fill out an online application that includes 3 short response essays (+1 optional essay), a high school transcript, a school profile, a resume, and an SAT/ACT score report. Applications are due at 11:59 PM on July 1st.

Name: Kristinspiration Scholarship
Subject: N/A
Description: The Kristinspiration scholarship is a $1,000 opportunity for anyone seeking to be the first in their family to pursue higher education. The scholarship aims to support these kinds of students and allow for them to pave the way to higher education for future generations of their family. In order to apply, students must be female high school seniors or undergraduate students, and must be a first-generation college student when they apply. Alongside these prerequisites, students must also explain why education is important to them and what legacy they hope to leave. The selection criteria, based on the essay, involve ambition, drive, and impact. The deadline to submit is June 30th, with the winners announced on August 1st.

Name: FXB Climate Advocates
Subject: STEM
Description: The FXB Climate Advocates program is a global youth climate advocacy initiative that aims to inform, empower, and mobilize young people to create climate solutions in their communities. Participants join a 4-month virtual program featuring workshops on climate science, policy, advocacy, digital storytelling, renewable energy, and sustainability, while receiving mentorship to develop and implement their own climate action projects. The program has engaged 1,000+ advocates from over 90 countries and supported 350+ youth-led climate projects. The website currently lists a Spring 2026 cohort with applications open, although a specific deadline and start date have not been announced. The program is open to youth climate advocates worldwide and operates entirely online, allowing participants from around the globe to collaborate and take action on climate issues.

Name: Collaborative Summer Research Experience (CSR-x)
Subject: STEM
Description: The Collaborative Summer Research Experience (CSR-x) is a free online summer research program that connects high school students from around the world with interdisciplinary research opportunities across fields such as Data Science and Machine Learning, Biomedical and Health Sciences, Environmental Science, Cognitive Science, and Economics. Participants work with research mentors on projects while gaining experience in academic research, with strong projects receiving recognition and potential publication opportunities. The 2026 program runs from July 7 to August 14, 2026, with mentee applications due June 20, and placements announced on July 1. The program is open to high school students globally. CSR-x is conducted entirely online, allowing students worldwide to participate regardless of location.

Name: Autumn Leah Beemer Memorial Scholarship
Subject: Welding
Description: The Autumn Leah Beemer Memorial scholarship is a $1,000 opportunity for any high school senior or trade school student pursuing welding. This scholarship aims to carry on the legacy of Autumn Leah Beemer, who tragically passed away from injuries in a car accident at the age of eighteen. In order to apply, students must be seniors or trade school students who are pursuing welding. Additionally, female and first-generation students are preferred. In order to apply, applicants must introduce themselves and how they demonstrate Autumn’s values and hardwork. Alongside this, applicants must explain why they pursued welding and what their goals are in their career. The scholarship deadline is August 18th, and the two winners will be announced on September 19th.

Name: Rowan College ACE-celerate STEM Camp (New Jersey)
Subject: STEM
Description: The ACE-celerate STEM Summer Camp is a free two-week STEM enrichment program hosted by Rowan College of South Jersey for Cumberland County students entering grades 9–12 in Fall 2026. The program focuses on energy and climate science through hands-on STEM projects, interactive challenges, and real-world learning experiences designed to help students build technical skills and explore future career pathways. Camp participants will have access to college-level facilities, including the Mechatronics Innovation Learning Lab (MILL), and will take part in chaperoned field trips and collaborative activities. The camp will be held August 10–14 and August 17–21, 2026, from 9:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. each weekday at the Rowan College of South Jersey Cumberland Campus. Students selected for the program must attend the full two-week session. Breakfast, lunch, camp materials, and program swag are provided at no cost. Due to limited capacity, only 50 students will be selected to participate. Applicants must be Cumberland County students entering grades 9–12 in Fall 2026, and the application deadline is July 9, 2026.

Name: DemocraShe Fall 2026
Subject: Education
Description: DemocraShe Fall 2026 is a free virtual leadership and civic engagement program for female-identifying students in grades 9–12. The program runs for 10 weeks beginning in September 2026, with participants meeting on Zoom for two hours each week. Through interactive workshops, students develop skills in public speaking, advocacy, community leadership, and resilience while connecting with peers from across the country. Participants may also receive mentorship, create a three-year action plan, and gain access to alumnae events, clubs, and networking opportunities. The program is fully remote and provides stipends to all participants. Applicants must be female-identifying high school students in grades 9–12, and the application deadline is July 15, 2026.

Name: Institute for Youth in Policy (YIP) Fellowship
Subject: Education
Description: Institute for Youth in Policy (YIP) Fellowship is a free, fully virtual public policy and civic engagement program for students ages 13–23 who are interested in social impact, advocacy, community organizing, and public policy. The fellowship lasts approximately two months and requires participants to attend two 1.5-hour meetings each week, held on Wednesdays at 5:00 PM PST and Saturdays at 9:00 AM PST, along with an additional 6–10 hours per weekdedicated to a capstone project. Fellows engage with guest speakers working in government, advocacy, and public policy, while developing research, leadership, and policy analysis skills. The program is free to participate in, though no stipend is provided. To successfully complete the fellowship, participants must attend at least 80% of sessions and complete all required assignments. Eligibility is limited to U.S.-based high school and undergraduate students, and the program is designed to accommodate students across Eastern, Central, and Pacific time zones.

Name: Sound+Science Summer Program
Subject: STEM
Description: The Sound+Science Summer Program is a strong opportunity for anyone seeking to gain experience in musical production or the usage of AI. Sound+Science is a program that is under the Simons Foundation’s Science Sandbox initiative, which aims to improve access to scientific and technology-based education for all students. In the Sound+Summer program, students will be able to further their experience in coding with Python, learning how to make music with AI, as well as developing their own personal projects. In order to apply, students must provide personal and contact information in the “Apply” section of the Sound+Summer website. Additionally, the program is solely accessible for students in the NYC public high school system. The sessions for the program are on Mondays and Wednesdays from 4 to 6 PM at 1 Rivington Street in Manhattan.

Name: Columbia Undergraduate Law Review Highschool Essay Contest
Subject: Law
Description: The Columbia Undergraduate Law Review High School Essay Contest is an international legal essay competition focused on immigration law, legal protections for non-citizens, and national sovereignty, requiring participants to submit an original essay responding to the prompt with no more than 1,500 words, referencing at least one court case or legal document and uploaded as a PDF through the competition’s submission form. The contest is open to all current high school students worldwide, while recent graduates are not eligible. Submissions are due by June 26, 2026, with essays reviewed in July and results expected during the first week of August. The competition is conducted entirely online through the Columbia Undergraduate Law Review website

Name: Young Filmmakers Contest 2026
Subject: Arts
Description: The One Earth Young Filmmakers Contest is an international environmental film competition that invites students to create short films about sustainability topics such as climate, energy, food, transportation, waste, water, or wildlife and ecosystems, with entries required to be 3-8 minutes long or at least 45 seconds for animation or stop-motion films. The contest is open to students from Grade 3 through age 25, including both US and international participants. Submissions are due by June 25, 2026, with winning films premiering on September 27, 2026 and later being screened at the One Earth Film Festival in April of the following year. Films are submitted online through FilmFreeway (on their website), while selected entries are showcased at One Earth Film Festival events.

Name: Rooted In The City Internship
Subject: Environmental
Description: The Rooted in the City program is a 11-month paid internship that explores land knowledge, local plants, creativity, and community-based ecological learning through monthly meetups, independent exploration, and a youth-led public presentation titled “Moving Through Our Senses with the Plant World.” It is open to high school and college-aged youth ages 14-24 who are New York City residents and able to travel throughout the city. The application deadline is June 29, 2025, with the program running from September 6, 2025, through June 6, 2026. Activities take place across all five boroughs of New York City, including locations such as Bronx Foodway, Central Park, Prospect Park, Governors Island, and other community and ecological sites.

Name: Bick New York Scholarship
Subject: N/A
Description: The Bick New York scholarship is a $30,000 opportunity with 6 winners created in honor of Marcia Bick Herman, a mathematics teacher known best for her belief that every student has the potential to succeed academically. Description: The Brian Chellios Memorial Scholarship is a $2,000 opportunity with 4 winners created in honor of Brian Chellios, a fire chief who passed away at 25 years old. He devoted much of his life towards the fire service, having served since he was 15 years old. The scholarship aims to honor the life of Brian Chellios by supporting the next generation of brave fire service workers. In order to apply, students must be high school seniors, undergraduates, or trade school students pursuing fire science, fire service, or EMS with a minimum of a 3.0 GPA. Additionally, in 600 words or less, students must also respond to what it means to belong to the fire service and to succeed in the path. The application deadline is January 1st, 2027 and the winners will be announced on February 2nd, 2027.
